name: Tata Nexon Facelift
overview: The Tata Nexon facelift elevates the compact SUV segment with an aggressive futuristic front fascia, bi-LED projector headlamps, a 10.25-inch floating touchscreen, and uncompromising 5-star crash safety build.
pros: Top-class 5-star safety rating
Striking concept-car styling
Punchy turbo petrol and diesel options
Feature-loaded cabin with 360-degree camera
cons: Infotainment software can have occasional lag
Firm low-speed ride quality
Rear seat headroom average for very tall passengers

name: Mahindra XUV700
overview: Mahindra XUV700 sets the benchmark in full-size mid-segment SUVs, offering dual 10.25-inch superscreens, Level-2 ADAS driver assistance, optional AWD, and blistering powertrain performance.
pros: Blistering 2.0L Turbo Petrol & 2.2L Diesel engines
Segment-first Level 2 ADAS suite
Comfortable 3-row layout and Sony 3D sound system
High speed stability and composure
cons: Long waiting periods for top variants
Third row best suited for children
Boot space with all 3 rows up is limited

name: Hyundai Creta
overview: The Hyundai Creta is India's undisputed king of mid-size SUVs, featuring bold parametric jewel grille, panoramic sunroof, ventilated front seats, dual-zone climate control, and refined driving dynamics.
pros: Silky smooth refined petrol & diesel engine choices
Plush premium cabin ergonomics
Panoramic sunroof and ventilated seats
High resale value and widespread service network
cons: Safety score behind Tata/Mahindra rivals
No manual option on the top turbo-petrol spec
Ride can feel soft at aggressive cornering speeds

name: Maruti Suzuki Swift
overview: The 4th generation Maruti Suzuki Swift brings the brand new Z-series 3-cylinder engine delivering astounding real-world fuel economy exceeding 25 kmpl, standard 6 airbags, and nimble city handling.
pros: Phenomenal fuel efficiency (25+ kmpl)
Nimble dimensions perfect for city traffic
6 Airbags standard across all trims
Peppy low-end throttle response
cons: Three-cylinder engine has slight idle vibration
Rear seat knee room is modest
Interior plastics feel utilitarian in places

name: BMW 3 Series Gran Limousine
overview: The BMW 3 Series Gran Limousine combines the legendary rear-wheel-drive dynamics of BMW with an extended 110mm wheelbase for unmatched rear-seat lounge luxury and class-leading curved display cockpit.
pros: Effortless 255 bhp TwinPower Turbo engine
First-class rear seat legroom and headrest cushions
Curved iDrive 8 display with wireless CarPlay
Peerless rear-wheel-drive balance and steering feel
cons: Low ground clearance requires caution on tall breakers
Premium pricing with no spare wheel well
Heftier road footprint than standard 3 Series

name: Tata Curvv EV
overview: The Tata Curvv EV introduces the Coupe-SUV body style to the mass market with striking aerodynamic sloping roofline, 55 kWh battery pack, ultra-fast 70 kW DC charging, and Level-2 ADAS suite.
pros: Stunning Coupe SUV silhouette and road presence
Claimed 585 km range with 55 kWh battery pack
Powered gesture tailgate and massive 500L boot
Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) and Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) charging
cons: Coupe roofline slightly compromises rear rearward visibility
Higher variant price approaches larger EV options
Piano black interior finishes prone to fingerprints

name: Tata Punch
overview: India's highest selling micro-SUV, the Tata Punch delivers authentic SUV stance, 187mm ground clearance, 90-degree opening doors, and certified 5-star crash safety at an unbeatable price point.
pros: Full 5-star GNCAP adult safety rating
Tough build quality and commanding road stance
90-degree wide opening doors for easy entry/exit
Available in Petrol, CNG, and EV options
cons: Engine lacks punch at high expressway speeds
AMT gearbox feels sluggish during overtakes
3-cylinder engine note audible under hard acceleration

name: Mahindra Thar
overview: The iconic Mahindra Thar is India's premier lifestyle off-roader with true 4x4 capability, mechanical locking differentials, convertible or hard-top roofs, and imposing road presence.
pros: Unmatched off-road prowess with 4x4 low range
Cult status design and massive street presence
Powerful mStallion petrol and mHawk diesel motors
Factory fitted hard-top and convertible options
cons: Bumpy ladder-frame ride quality on uneven roads
Ingress to rear seats requires folding front passenger seat
Very limited luggage boot space

name: Mahindra Thar Electric (Vision Thar.e)
overview: The Mahindra Thar.e concept is a radical electric off-roader based on the INGLO-born EV platform with modular geometric design, high ground clearance, quad-motor electronic 4WD, and futuristic cabin tech.
pros: Revolutionary electric 4x4 with instant torque
INGLO platform with 80 kWh high-density battery
Aggressive futuristic cyberpunk styling
Clean zero-emission overland off-roading
cons: Expected launch slated for 2026-2027
Higher price point compared to ICE Thar
Remote trail charging infrastructure dependency

name: Mahindra XUV 3XO EV
overview: Mahindra's all-new electrified compact SUV based on the acclaimed XUV 3XO platform, featuring a panoramic skyroof, dual 10.25-inch screens, Level-2 ADAS, and blistering 0-100 km/h acceleration.
pros: Largest panoramic sunroof in the compact EV segment
Level 2 ADAS suite with radar and 360-degree camera
Class-leading cabin width and rear legroom
Fast DC charging from 10% to 80% in 30 mins
cons: Boot space slightly compromised by battery packaging
Polarizing front LED light signature
Real-world highway range may vary under heavy AC load

name: Hyundai Venue
overview: The Hyundai Venue combines dark chrome parametric grille, connected LED taillamps, 2-step reclining rear seats, and SmartSense Level-1 ADAS into a compact, tech-rich city SUV package.
pros: Refined 1.0L Turbo petrol engine paired with DCT
Level 1 ADAS safety features introduced in top trims
User-friendly BlueLink connected car tech with 60+ features
2-step rear seat recline function
cons: Rear seat space tight for three full-sized adults
No diesel-automatic transmission combination
Firm suspension over broken potholes

name: Hyundai i20
overview: The Hyundai i20 is India's benchmark premium hatchback, boasting parametric jewel design, 10.25-inch touchscreen, Bose 7-speaker sound system, electric sunroof, and 6 standard airbags.
pros: Gorgeous low-slung European hatchback styling
Plush cabin with 10.25-inch infotainment and Bose audio
Generous rear knee room and wide shoulder room
Standard 6 airbags across all variants
cons: Top variants are priced close to compact SUVs
Diesel engine discontinued
Low seating posture might not appeal to SUV enthusiasts

name: Hyundai Verna
overview: The 6th generation Hyundai Verna is a sensational mid-size sedan offering a 160 hp turbo-petrol motor, full Level-2 ADAS suite, 5-star GNCAP safety rating, and fastback styling.
pros: Ferocious 160 hp 1.5L Turbo engine (0-100 in 8.1s)
Full 5-star GNCAP adult and child safety score
Spacious rear legroom and huge 528-litre boot
Dual integrated curved displays and heated/ventilated seats
cons: Futuristic horizontal LED bar styling is polarizing
Rear headroom limited for 6ft+ passengers due to fastback roof
Low ground clearance on large speed breakers

name: Maruti Suzuki Dzire
overview: The 2025 Maruti Suzuki Dzire redefines the compact sedan segment with a historic 5-star GNCAP safety rating, electric sunroof, 360-degree camera, wireless Apple CarPlay, and class-best 25.7 kmpl mileage.
pros: Historic 5-star GNCAP crash test rating
Segment-first electric sunroof and 360 camera
Extraordinary fuel efficiency of 25.7 kmpl
Plush dual-tone beige interior with rear AC vents
cons: 3-cylinder Z-Series engine has moderate top-end punch
Rear middle seat best for children
Long waiting period on top variants

name: Maruti Suzuki Brezza
overview: The Maruti Suzuki Brezza is India's trusted family compact SUV, powered by the reliable 1.5L K-Series DualJet engine, Head-Up Display (HUD), 360-degree camera, electric sunroof, and paddle shifters.
pros: Super reliable 4-cylinder 1.5L naturally aspirated engine
Smooth 6-speed torque converter AT with paddle shifters
Segment-first Head-Up Display (HUD) and 360 camera
Low maintenance costs and massive resale value
cons: No turbo-petrol or diesel engine options
Cabin plastics feel slightly dated compared to rivals
Top variants enter mid-size SUV price bracket
